title: Design a Search / Retrieval System
interviewAnswer: A search system typically has document ingestion/indexing, query understanding, first-stage lexical/vector retrieval, optional reranking, caching and offline/online evaluation. The design should state latency, freshness and relevance objectives.
why: Design a Search / Retrieval System appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: A search system typically has document ingestion/indexing, query understanding, first-stage lexical/vector retrieval, optional reranking, caching and offline/online evaluation. The design should state latency, freshness and relevance objectives. Candidate recall vs reranking precision. Hybrid exact/semantic retrieval. Query/log privacy. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Technical documentation search using BM25 + ANN candidates followed by cross-encoder reranking.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Design a Search / Retrieval System make?
How would you validate or debug Design a Search / Retrieval System in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
